provenance.orgName: Hyde (Hida, formerly New Minster, Winchester), Hampshire, Benedictine abbey of Holy Trinity, St Mary the Virgin, and St Peter
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records the following context for the rejection:

Written in Hyde abbey (no. 54 in catalogue for an exhibition in Winchester College library, 31 March - 8 April 1936). This is chiefly conjectured chiefly because of the close resemblance of the decoration to that of the Liber de Hyda. But there is no reason to suppose that this was executed at Hyde and not by professional Winchester decorators.

provenance.orgName: Winchester, Hampshire, College of St Mary the Virgin of Winchester
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records the following context for the rejection: There seems to be no reason to identify this book with the manuscript referred to in Bursar accounts for 1436-7. Compare Oakeshott, The Library, 5th series ix (1954), pp. 15-16.

history.provenance: [Information from index card for rejected Hyde attribution; text partially obscured by hole]: Traditionally the book is one of those taken from the Cathedral library in the Civil Wars and given to the College Library. Most not were restored later but not apparently the Concordantia. See the list [...] in the College Benefactors book.
